caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

The horizontal axis represents sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80%, and is labeled as "Sparsity Rate". The axis is linear and displays values in increments of 10%, with categories arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis represents perplexity, measured in logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 10^0 to 10^3. The axis is labeled "Perplexity" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with tick marks at powers of 10, indicating values of 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The chart features two data series: a blue column representing "Per-Output" perplexity and an orange column representing "Per-Layer" perplexity. The Per-Output column reaches a maximum value of approximately 50 at a sparsity rate of 70%, while the Per-Layer column reaches a maximum value of approximately 25 at the same sparsity rate. Both columns exhibit a general downward trend with increasing sparsity rates, but diverge significantly at higher sparsity levels. The Per-Output column consistently maintains a slightly higher perplexity value compared to the Per-Layer column throughout the range of sparsity rates.
